_comment: Hand-authored. Bank 3: the password check menu and editor ($870D-$8B6A). The generators subtract these.

regions.name: WINDOW OPENING (`$8B7E`): hide the cursors, set the first box (`$8B7E`)
WINDOW OPENING (`$8B7E`): draw a frame
regions.description: `JSR $8BB3` with A = `$6C` (non-zero: draw the frame tiles). A frame of Y = 15 or more ends the routine, **so the last frame stays**.

regions.name: WINDOW OPENING (`$8B7E`): erase it
regions.description: `JSR $8BB3` with A = 0: the same frame redrawn in blank tiles (`$20`) - **only the frame's own tiles are blanked, the inside is never touched**. The next, bigger frame is queued behind it.

regions.name: WINDOW OPENING (`$8B7E`): grow
regions.description: Y := 1 if it was 0, else Y + 2 (Y runs 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15); X += 2 (X runs 6, 8 ... 22); the address -= `$21` (one row up, one column left; `BNE` is always taken as `$19` stays non-zero). **Eight steps from a box 8 x 2 at row 11 to one 24 x 17 at `$2064` (row 3, column 4).** RUN: it returns after 16 frames with the queue still holding the last row; the frame's bounding box goes rows 10-10 -> 8-14 -> 6-16 -> 4-17 -> 3-19 and columns 11-20 -> 4-27, and the final nametable is the frame of 24 x 17 tiles around the grid (the characters start at PPU `$2086`, row 4 column 6).

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): draw or blank a frame
regions.description: Entry: `$19:$18` = the PPU address of its top-left tile, **X = the inner width, Y = the inner height**, A = 0 for a blank frame (`$1B`; `$8C76` then returns `$20` for every tile), any other value for the real tiles. The frame is (X + 2) x (Y + 2) tiles and **nothing inside it is drawn**. RUN: X = 4, Y = 2 gave rows `07 03 03 03 03 0B / 05 .. 0A / 05 .. 0A / 0D 0C 0C 0C 0C 0E`; X = 0, Y = 1 gave `07 0B / 05 0A / 0D 0E`. The top-left corner (tile `$07`) is queued first.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): top edge
regions.description: `$15` := X; if X is non-zero, `$18`++ and a run of X tiles `$03` along the row (`JSR $C036` = `$D5F8`: a PPU queue run with count `$15`, tile `$14`; bit 7 of the count = increment 32), `$18`--.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): top-right corner
regions.description: The left address is saved, `$18` += X + 1 (the `SEC` before `ADC`), and tile `$0B` is queued; then `$19` is saved too.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): side edges, if Y is non-zero
regions.description: `$15` := Y OR `$80` (a vertical run of Y), one row down (`JSR $C0E7` = `$DA1D`: the address + `$20`, wrapping past the nametable), tile `$0A` down the right side; then the left address is restored, one row down again and Y tiles `$05` down the left side.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): bottom row
regions.description: The left address is restored and saved again; for Y non-zero `$15` := Y and the address steps down Y + 1 rows (`$C0E7` once, then once per count) to the bottom row, and tile `$0D` is queued there. **For Y = 0 none of the side and corner code runs, so the bottom row's edge and right corner are laid over the top row and its left corner stays the top-left `07`** (RUN: `07 0C 0C 0C 0C 0E`) - why the opening animation's first box is not a real box.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): bottom edge and corner
regions.description: For X non-zero a run of X tiles `$0C` and, at `$18` + X + 1, the corner `$0E`; the caller's address is restored and Y = height comes back in Y. `RTS`.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): choose a tile (`$8C76`)
regions.description: `ROR $1B / ROL $1B` leaves `$1B` unchanged and sets the flags: non-zero returns A (the tile asked for), zero returns `$20`.

regions.name: WINDOW FRAME (`$8BB3`, the password screen's boxes): queue one tile (`$8C7F`)
regions.description: Reserve 4 bytes (`JSR $C04B` = `$D6D3`, waiting for room), take the queue offset (`$C03C`) in Y and write `[count 1][$19][$18]`; the caller stores the tile at `$0103,Y` and commits with `JSR $C03F`. Y is clobbered (the height is kept in `$1A`).
